claims.text: Placebo treatment reduced both social and physical pain, and increased activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) in both modalities
claims.evidence: Direct experimental finding from fMRI study comparing placebo vs control groups

claims.text: Effects on behavior were mediated by a pathway connecting dlPFC to the PAG
claims.evidence: Three-path mediation analysis showed dlPFC mediates placebo effects via PAG activity

claims.text: Placebo altered the relationship between affect and both dlPFC and PAG activity during social pain
claims.evidence: Moderated Path b effects showed different brain-affect relationships in placebo vs control groups

claims.text: Placebo effects on physical pain depend on pathways connecting prefrontal cortex and periaqueductal gray (PAG)
claims.evidence: Based on established models and confirmed by current mediation findings

claims.text: Opioidergic PAG activity is implicated in the regulation of social pain
claims.evidence: Referenced from recent work (Hsu et al., 2013) and supported by current PAG findings

claims.text: Activation patterns in dlPFC mediating placebo effects are modality-specific for social versus physical pain
claims.evidence: SVM classifier achieved 80% accuracy discriminating social vs physical pain placebo patterns in dlPFC

claims.text: Placebo treatment reduced expression of a multivariate social rejection-specific brain pattern
claims.evidence: Significant decrease in rejection pattern expression in placebo vs control group post-intervention

claims.text: Under control treatment, dlPFC, vmPFC/OFC/rACC, and PAG activities were associated with more negative affect, but after placebo treatment, activity in these regions was associated with reduced negative affect
claims.evidence: Path b moderation effects showed opposite brain-affect correlations between groups

claims.text: Multilevel mediation analysis can identify mechanistic pathways underlying placebo effects by testing relationships between treatment, brain activity, and behavioral outcomes
claims.evidence: Novel analytical framework successfully identified three-step mechanistic pathways (Paths a, b, ab)

claims.text: Individuals who experience a targeted romantic rejection are 20 times more likely to develop depression than the general population
